$comment: Riftlight, Restless Coast key node (docs/campaigns/continental-rift/arc.md, buried-bridge; design note buried-bridge-playtest.md). Rewritten in November 2026 for the campaign rewrite after the pilot (riftlight-bone-yard). Question: where did this bridge's river go? Puddle carries it, Orin is on stage and Pip voices Lady Olivia's ideas. The p1 (old_river) is that the bridge stands where a river ran when the land had an older shape: the Coast fragment, fragment_coast_learned, set on every path. orin_chime_shared is a real choice: sharing gives Orin the readings and costs the chime's help at the tide; keeping it means Orin climbs to measure by hand. The arches are gray stone with white specks, like salt on bread, with a waterline carved high up, which The Borrowed Ruins recognizes. The sealed door stays sealed.
title: A Bridge Without a River

plate.narration: Stone arches rise from the silt beside a dry channel. No river passes under them now. From the firm bank, the old bridge stretches away into a haze of salt and pale mud.

goal.text: Where did this bridge's river go?

steps.label: Save what you can from the tide
Work out what the bridge remembers

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny and a little spooky, with real consequences. Short sentences. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel. The bridge is a mystery to witness, not to explain; the sealed door stays sealed. Nobody dies.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.saltrot_guide: Puddle, the Skupper guide (she/her). Quick, chatty and cheerfully blunt. Guides from pools and channels, signals with her crest, puffs up round when startled and stings a little. Keeps her lunch in a floating box. Wants to find out why her flats keep moving, and to keep her grandmother's rule: show the bank, never the stone.
npcVoices.Master Orin Vale: Griffin scholar and Riftseeker (he/him). Kind, dusty, delighted by evidence and a little sad about sandwiches. Wants to understand before anyone forces anything.
npcVoices.Pip Thistledown: Young manticore scout (he/him). Eager, notebook always out, quotes "Lady Olivia says..." and tries her ideas. Wants to bring Lady Olivia something amazing.

walk_out.narration: Puddle leads you upriver from Tidepocket, pool to pool. "Grandmother says there's a bridge out here with no river under it," she says. "A bridge needs a river. So where did this one's river go?" She stops where the brown mud ends. Ahead lies cold gray silt, soft as porridge, and past it, the old bank. "I swim. You don't. Pick your way."

choices.label: Hop the stones Puddle points at

check_hop.narration: "That one. That one. Not that one!" Puddle points with a fin from the channel. The stones are small and far apart.
check_hop.prompt: Hop from stone to stone across the soft silt

onSuccess.narration: Stone, stone, wobble, stone. Puddle counts you across like a race.

check_posts.narration: Old stone posts stick up out of the silt in a crooked line, the ones Dab saw. Someone set them here long ago, beside something.
check_posts.prompt: Work out which posts stand on firm ground, and follow them

onSuccess.narration: Post to post, firm all the way. "They used to mark a riverbank," says Puddle, surprised.

fly_rope.narration: Your flier hops the silt in two flaps and ties a rope to a post on the far side. Everyone else crosses hand over hand. Puddle swims underneath, cheering. "Do it again!"

walk_stuck.narration: The silt swallows you to the knees and holds on. Puddle puffs up like a ball and floats beside you. You grab her, carefully, and she tows you out. "Ow. Spines. You're welcome." You reach the bank wet to the waist.

bank.narration: From the bank, you finally see it. A bridge stands over a dry riverbed. Its arches are gray stone with white specks, like salt on bread, with a waterline carved high up. Not a drop of water under them. A little snow falls on the far end, from a clear sky. Master Orin Vale is here already, brushing an arch. Most of the dust lands on him. "Ah! You've come about the river too," he says.

choices.label: Ask Orin what he has found

orin.narration: Orin holds up a jar of pale grit. "Glacier silt, under a bridge with no river. And my map has no river here at all." He looks at your pack, where the Listening Chime hums. "Lend me your chime while we work, and I can measure which way it leans all day. But it will be on my pole, not with you." Puddle flicks her crest. "Or keep it, and he measures that waterline by hand. Up there."

choices.label: Share the chime's readings with Orin

share.narration: You hand Orin the Listening Chime. He hangs it from his measuring pole, and at once it leans north, up the dry riverbed, toward the glacier. It stays leaning. Orin writes very fast. "Thank you. You'll have it back before supper. Probably." "He means definitely," Puddle tells you. "Right, Orin?"

keep.narration: You keep the chime in your pack, where it hums to itself. Orin nods, only a little sad. "Then I'll measure the old waterline by hand." He looks up at it. It is very high. "Hm," he says. "Hm," agrees Puddle.

pip_runs.narration: Feet thump along the bank. It's Pip Thistledown, the young manticore scout, notebook flapping. He doesn't stop. He runs onto the first arch, toward a round stone door sealed shut at the far end. "Lady Olivia says rules are for people who haven't looked yet!" The old stone creaks. Puddle's crest shoots up. "Off the stone! Show the bank, never the stone!"

choices.label: Talk to him, manticore to manticore

check_call.narration: Pip wobbles on the arch with one foot up, like a heron who has made a mistake.
check_call.prompt: Call Pip back to the bank before the stone shifts

onSuccess.narration: "Okay. Okay! Bank." Pip tiptoes back the way he came.

check_grab.narration: Pip is three steps out. His tail swishes back and forth, right in front of you.
check_grab.prompt: Grab Pip by the tail and pull him back to the bank

onSuccess.narration: You catch his tail and reel him in like a kite.

manticore_call.narration: You flick your tail the polite manticore way, low and slow. Pip's ears go pink. He tiptoes back to the bank without a word.

pip_back.narration: Behind Pip, a loose stone slides off the arch and plops into the riverbed. Puddle lets her crest down, slowly. "Thank you," she tells you. "Grandmother would have puffed so hard she floated away." Pip draws the sealed door instead. "Lady Olivia would want to know what's behind it." "Nobody knows," says Orin. "And today, nobody will."

pip_falls.narration: The arch shrugs. Pip slides off it, and you slide after him, down into the dry riverbed in a shower of silt. Pip sits up with a pebble in each ear. "River pebbles!" he says. Up on the bank, Puddle's crest lies flat. "You walked on the stone," she says quietly. "I'll have to tell Grandmother."

choices.label: Climb out and look under the arches

silt_choice.narration: Under the lowest arch, silt is packed to the top like stuffing in a pillow. "Dig it out!" says Pip. "Lady Olivia says a good shove saves a whole day." Puddle shakes her head. "The tide scours that groove twice a day. Open the little dam and let the water wash it. Slower, and wetter." Orin looks from one to the other. "Shovels scrape old stone. Waves soak old scholars."

choices.label: Let the tide wash it out
Let your bigfoot scoop it out
Let your thornguard shore up the arch

check_dig.narration: Everyone grabs a shovel from Orin's kit. Pip grabs a spoon.
check_dig.prompt: Dig the silt out from under the arch, fast

dug_out.narration: The silt flies. In no time the arch is clear. But a shovel scraped the stone, and a row of old carvings under the arch is scratched to gray dust. Orin winces. "Fast," he says. "And sad."

dug_slow.narration: The silt slumps back twice. You dig with your hands in the end, and your arms ache. When the arch is finally clear, a row of old carvings under it is scratched to gray dust where the shovels hit. Orin winces. "Slow, and sad," he says.

bigfoot_smash.narration: Your bigfoot scoops silt out in huge armfuls, like a bear at a honey pot. The arch is clear in no time. But one big paw scraped the stone, and a row of old carvings is rubbed to gray dust. "Strong," says Orin. "And sad."

thornguard_brace.narration: Your thornguard braces the arch with a shield while everyone digs around it, gently. Not one shovel touches the stone. "Now that," says Orin, "is how you dig." Pip digs with his spoon, very carefully, to prove he can.

wash_out.narration: Puddle sits on the little dam of shells across the groove. "When the wave reaches me, shout NOW and I pull. Too soon, and it only splashes."

interaction.cue: Shout now when the wave reaches the dam.

washed.narration: WHOOSH. The wave races under the arch, and the silt slides out like porridge from a pot. The old carvings underneath come out clean. So do you. Everyone is soaked to the ears. "Told you," says Puddle. "Wetter."

washed_twice.narration: Too soon. Splash, and only half the silt goes. You wait for the next wave, standing in it, while Pip hums to keep warm. The carvings come out clean. You come out cold and very wet.

under_arch.narration: Under the arch, smooth river pebbles cover the bottom, round as eggs. Dry water weed hangs from the stone like an old wet beard. And high up, higher than Orin's head, the waterline is carved deep. "That's no tide mark," says Puddle. "Tides don't reach that high. Not even angry ones."

variants.text: Below it, the row of carvings is scratched to dust. Nobody will ever know what they showed.
Below it runs a row of carved fish, all swimming the same way: north, up the dry riverbed.

measure.narration: Orin wants to know exactly how high that waterline is, to set beside his map. "How deep was the river?" he asks the arch. The arch does not answer.

variants.text: Your chime still dangles from his measuring pole, leaning north.
Without the chime on his pole, he will have to climb up and measure it himself.

choices.label: Hold Orin's pole up to the line

check_pole.narration: The pole is very long, and the chime on top swings north every time you move it.
check_pole.prompt: Hold the long pole steady against the waterline while Orin reads it

onSuccess.narration: "Two griffins and a beak high," Orin reads, and writes it down.

onFailure.narration: The pole wobbles, and its end bonks Orin on the beak. The number he reads is mostly a guess.

check_spot.narration: Orin climbs the arch one talon at a time, tongue out. The old stone is slippery with silt.
check_spot.prompt: Stand under Orin and catch him if he slips

onSuccess.narration: He reads the mark, slips on the way down, and lands in your arms. "Thank you. Two griffins and a beak high."

onFailure.narration: He slips halfway. You catch most of him, and the rest lands on you. The number he shouts on the way down is only a guess.

check_count.narration: The arch is built in neat rows of stone, each as tall as a loaf of bread.
check_count.prompt: Count the stone rows from the riverbed up to the waterline

onSuccess.narration: Twenty-two rows. Orin does the sum in his head, then on his fingers, then in his notebook.

onFailure.narration: You lose count at seventeen, and again at nine. Pip helps, which makes it worse.

measured.narration: Orin writes the number in big letters. "A river ran this deep, under this bridge. Deeper than the tallest yeti." Pip writes it down too, then draws a yeti for scale.

measured_rough.narration: Orin writes the number with a question mark. "Near enough," he says, though his face says it isn't. "A deep river ran here, deeper than a yeti is tall." Pip draws a yeti, then a question mark.

samples.narration: Orin lines up three jars: brown Saltrot mud, pale glacier silt, and dust from the arch, gray with white specks. Puddle licks the arch dust. "Not Saltrot stone," she says. "Not glacier, either. I've licked most things, and I've never tasted this." Orin writes: stone from nowhere near here.

follow.narration: "Where did it go, though?" says Puddle, and points a fin up the dry riverbed. "Follow it and see. From the bank." The bank upstream is crumbly and steep. Pip has already started, of course.

choices.label: Follow Puddle's crest from the groove

check_follow.narration: Every third step, a lump of bank breaks off and rolls into the riverbed.
check_follow.prompt: Hurry along the crumbly bank without sliding down it

onSuccess.narration: You skip along the top, light as a gull.

onFailure.narration: The bank crumbles under you, and you slide halfway down on your bottom before Pip grabs your sleeve.

check_crest.narration: Puddle swims the trickle in the groove below. Crest up means stop. Crest flat means go. Crest wiggling means "I saw a snail."
check_crest.prompt: Read Puddle's crest signals and step only where she says

onSuccess.narration: Stop, go, go, snail, go. You never put a foot wrong.

onFailure.narration: You mix up stop and snail and step onto nothing. Down you slide, in a shower of silt.

riverbed_end.narration: A little way upstream, the dry riverbed runs straight into a grassy hill and stops. No pond. No waterfall. Just a hill, sitting where the river ran, as if it sat down there after. "Rivers don't do that," says Puddle. "Neither do hills," says Orin, frowning. Pip writes HILL? and underlines it.

tide.narration: Back at the bridge, the groove gurgles. The tide is coming in down the dry riverbed. Orin's drawings lie drying on the low shelf. Pip's notebook, full of drawings for Lady Olivia, sits open on a rock below. "There's time to reach one," says Puddle. "I can't carry paper. I'm a fish. Mostly." Orin looks at his drawings. Pip looks at his notebook.

choices.label: Follow the chime along the old stone

save_drawings.narration: The water slides toward the low shelf, quiet as a cat. The top drawing lifts at one corner.
save_drawings.prompt: Snatch Orin's drawings off the low shelf before the water does

save_notebook.narration: The water is already around the rock. Pip's notebook flaps its pages like it wants to swim.
save_notebook.prompt: Splash out and snatch Pip's notebook off the rock

check_footing.narration: In your pack, the chime hums louder over old stone. Under the silt, the bridge's footing runs along the riverbed like a hidden path.
check_footing.prompt: Follow the chime's hum along the buried footing and reach both

onFailure.narration: The hum fades halfway, and so does the footing. You reach Pip's notebook and fall in. Orin's drawings float away.

drawings_saved.narration: Every page, dry. Orin hugs them like a baby bird. Below, the water lifts Pip's notebook off its rock and carries it away, pages flapping. Pip watches it go. "My drawings for Lady Olivia," he says, very small.

drawings_soaked.narration: You grab the pages, but a wave grabs half of them back. Orin wrings out what's left. "Useful," he says. "Just less exact." Below, Pip's notebook floats away too. Pip doesn't say anything at all.

notebook_saved.narration: You hold the notebook over your head, dry as toast. Pip hugs it, and then you. Up on the shelf, Orin's drawings float off one by one. He fishes out a soggy page. "Redrawn from memory, then," he sighs. "Useful. Just less exact."

notebook_soggy.narration: You come up dripping, with Pip's notebook in your teeth. Half his drawings have run into inky smudges. "Lady Olivia likes smudges," Pip says bravely. Orin's drawings are gone downstream. "From memory, then," he sighs. "Less exact."

both_saved.narration: Hum, step, hum, step. You run the hidden footing, scoop up Orin's pages and Pip's notebook, and run back with water at your heels. "The chime knew the old stone," says Orin, amazed. "It knew where the bridge stood."

flood.narration: The tide fills the old riverbed, just for a while. For the first time in who knows how long, water runs under the arches. The bridge stands in it, gray and speckled, looking exactly right. Puddle swims under the middle arch and back, grinning. "It fits," she says. "Like a puddle."

pip_after.narration: Pip flips through his notebook, page after page of pebbles and arches. "Lady Olivia will see what this place used to be!" he says. Orin raises an eyebrow, and lets it go.

variants.text: Pip sits on the bank with his chin in his paws. "Lady Olivia will think I found nothing." Puddle pokes him with one fin, gently. "You found a bridge. Draw it again." He sniffs, and starts.
Puddle still isn't quite looking at Pip, or at you.

choices.label: Climb to the high bank and rest

rest.narration: On the high bank, Puddle opens her floating lunch box: kelp rolls wrapped in leaves. "Guides eat first," she says, and does. Orin shares his sandwiches, slightly squashed. Across the water, the round stone door at the far end of the bridge sits sealed with silt and shells. "Well," says Orin, wiping his beak. "Shall I tell you what I think?"

choices.label: Listen to the sealed door first

door.narration: You sit very still and listen. When the wind blows across the water, the sealed door hums, low and soft. It is the same note as your chime. Pip stops chewing. Nobody knows what is behind that door, and Puddle says nobody should try. Orin writes it down and draws a very small question mark.

old_river.narration: Orin unrolls his map, the one with places that don't fit. He lays your findings beside it: the waterline, the river pebbles, the gray stone with white specks from nowhere near here, the riverbed that runs into a hill. "My map has no river here," he says. "But this bridge stood over one. A river ran right here, long ago, when the land was a different shape." Puddle stares. "The land had a different shape?" "One more piece that doesn't match today's map," says Orin softly. "But matches something older."

variants.text: Your exact measurement sits right beside it, two griffins and a beak high.

north.narration: Orin follows the lean with his eyes. "Glacier silt. Snow from a clear sky. Something up north is draining this way, through an opening somewhere. Something is moving things, and the land remembers where it used to be." Pip's eyes shine. "Imagine if we could use..." Puddle puffs up a little, and he stops.

variants.text: Orin gives your chime back. On its string it leans north, toward the glacier, harder than it has all day.
In your pack, the chime leans north, toward the glacier, harder than it has all day.

home.narration: The tide slides back out and leaves the riverbed shining. Puddle hops into the groove. "Home. Bank all the way. Nobody touch the stone."

variants.text: Your big heap of dug silt has slumped right across the high path, so it's the low way or nothing.

choices.label: Wade the low way with Puddle

check_high.narration: The high path is narrow, and the evening wind wants it more than you do.
check_high.prompt: Hop along the narrow high path without slipping

onSuccess.narration: You hop it like a hopscotch board. Puddle claps her fins.

onFailure.narration: A gust pushes you off the path and into a pool. It is a very small pool. You fit it exactly, like Puddle.

check_low.narration: The low way is knee-deep in fresh tide and cold, sticky silt.
check_low.prompt: Wade the low way, holding on to each other

onSuccess.narration: Squelch, squelch, step. Nobody lets go. Puddle swims beside you, humming.

onFailure.narration: The silt grabs your boots. Puddle puffs up round, and you ride the last bit on her. "Ow. Every time," she says.

ending.narration: At the edge of the flats, Puddle scratches the bridge into the mud for the guides' account: one bridge, one waterline, no river. Then she stops. Far out on the flats, something blinks: snow, nothing, snow. "That," says Puddle, "is new." So here is your piece: this bridge stands where a river ran when the land was a different shape. Something is moving the land. What is it? And can you put things right?

variants.text: Orin tucks your chime readings under his wing, to lay beside his map.
Orin has his notes, and a lot of questions. "I'll take your word for the lean," he says.
His copy says "near enough" at the top.
Pip runs ahead with his notebook, to show Lady Olivia.
Pip is drawing it all again from memory, for Lady Olivia.
Puddle has to tell Grandmother somebody walked on the stone. She's dreading it.
